rulers.note: Dethroned and imprisoned by Süleymanshah II.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Saltukids). Theodosiopolis (Erzurum) taken by the Seljuk Turks in 1071 and the beylik 'centred in Erzurum' to 1202. The Saltukids page gives no area for 1071; Erzurum province stands for the core.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Erzurum was briefly reoccupied by the Byzantine Empire between 1077 and 1079' (Saltukids page); the city is dropped, the rest of the province kept (the page does not say what else was held).
New keyframe. Back to the Erzurum core in 1079.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'At its height' the beylik included 'the entirety of present-day Erzurum and Bayburt provinces', lands east of Erzincan, 'most of Kars Province' and lands north of Ağrı and Muş (Saltukids page); it 'fought frequently against the Georgian Kingdom for hegemony of the Kars region' (1154, 1161, 1184 sieges). The undated height is placed at 1132 (Izz al-Din Saltuk becomes malik) at confidence 1; Ağrı and Muş fringes are not drawn.

ledger.note: 1071: after Manzikert the Seljuk Turks take Theodosiopolis (Erzurum); the Saltukid beylik is founded. 'In 1071, after the decisive battle at Manzikert, the Seljuk Turks took possession of Theodosiopolis'; 'The Saltukids ... ruled from 1071 to 1202'. The pages do not say the Byzantines held it before; that is the reading.
1077: the Byzantines reoccupy Erzurum ('Erzurum was briefly reoccupied by the Byzantine Empire between 1077 and 1079'). The Erzurum page does not mention it.
1079: the Byzantine reoccupation of Erzurum ends ('between 1077 and 1079').

ledger.note: Undated, placed at 1132 (Izz al-Din Saltuk becomes malik): 'At its height' the beylik held 'the entirety of present-day Erzurum and Bayburt provinces' and 'most of Kars Province'. The pages give no acquisition dates.

ledger.note: 1202: the Seljuks of Rum end the Saltukids. In 598/1202 Süleymanshah II, 'en route to a campaign against Georgia', 'put an end to the Saltuqids' and dethroned and imprisoned Alaeddin Muhammed (the Erzurum page dates the conquest to 1201). The sultanate-of-rum dossier records the 1202 gain.

ledger.note: 1202: the beylik is annexed by the Sultanate of Rum (infobox: disestablished 1202).

wars.name: Saltukid wars with Georgia

zones.text: Kars province, "most of" which the beylik held

wars.outcome: Izz al-Din was defeated and captured by Georgians under Dimitri I in 1154 (ransomed by the Artuqid Sökmen); in 1161 he and Turkish allies besieged the Georgians at Ani and were defeated; George III besieged Erzurum in 1184; the city 'repelled many attacks by the Seljuks and Georgians until 1201'.

wars.name: Rum conquest of Erzurum
wars.outcome: Süleymanshah II 'put an end to the Saltuqids' in 1202 (1201 on the Erzurum page).

certainty.note: Provinces stand for the beylik; the Georgian frontier on the Kars side moved with the wars and no line is given.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Disagreements: end 1202 (Saltukids page: 598/1202) vs 1201 (Erzurum page); Byzantine reoccupation 1077-1079 is on the Saltukids page only. Not settled: the extent before the undated 'height' (confidence 1 at 1132); Tortum and Oltu are not mentioned on the page; the Mengujekids are not mentioned on the Saltukids page. After 1202 Erzurum was an appanage of Tughril ibn Kilij Arslan II and Jahan Shah for about thirty years and Kay Qubadh I incorporated it in 1230 (the sultanate-of-rum dossier has these). The byzantine-empire dossier should carry the mirrors of the 1071 loss and the 1077-1079 reoccupation.
